One experiment that I did was trying to extract iron from other materials. I live in an area that is rich in volcanic material. I found out that plain old Basalt (that hard dark grey rock) that underlies Eastern Oregon, Northern Nevada and Southern Idaho is about 10% iron. It contains Fe2O3 (about 3%) and plain old FeO (about 7%).

What I did was get some Ceramic Crucibles to old the crushed basalt. I added some charcoal dust and mixed with the crushed basalt. When FeO and Fe2O3 are heated in the presents of carbon the carbon robs the Fe of the Oxygen atom making CO (Carbon Monoxide) This leaves free iron. Since Iron is the heaviest component of Basalt but one of the smaller contents you need a lot of basalt to reduce into iron. I finally got it down to workable iron but a couple of pounds of Basalt only yields a couple of ounces of iron. You you can see you will need a lot of fuel for the forge and a lot of basalt. But it was an interesting experiment.
